newsitem.title: USA: Texas lawmakers asked to merge regulatory agencies.
newsitem.headline: Texas lawmakers asked to merge regulatory agencies.

text.p: The chairman of the Texas Railroad Commission voiced support this week for a proposal to merge the agency with the state's Public Utility Commission as regulators prepare for continued deregulation of the electric and telecommunications industries.

"There's a revolution going on here and we need to understand it," Railroad Commission Chairman Charles Matthews said. "Texas elected officials (and) Texas regulators -- whether elected or appointed -- need to understand there are changes in the marketplace."

Matthews said the Railroad Commission has no regulatory authority over electric utilities, which could pose problems in a cold weather crisis where the commission has the power over gas utilities to redirect gas supplies.

Planned mergers of overlapping electric and gas utilities in the state -- Texas Utilities Co and ENSERCH Corp in Dallas and Houston Industries NorAm Energy Corp in Houston -- prompted regulators in the state to seek increased oversight on their impact on Texas consumers.
The Public Utility Commission separately is seeking regulatory authority from the legislature to oversee possible anti-competitive impacts of the mergers.
